title: Misty Western Ghats Valley
project: TODO: client, film, album or game this cue belongs to
brief: TODO: the words the client actually used, verbatim
audience: TODO: who hears it, where they hear it, and what they already know
purpose: a continuous 90-second slow orchestral adagio over the misty green valleys of the Western Ghats at dawn
point_of_view: narrator, not a character: the camera floats, it does not walk, so no pulse and no urgent register
job: set the place before the first word of voice-over
hold one unbroken mood: no key change, no drum
leave the middle of the spectrum free for the narration
end on the note it began, so the cut out is not a shock
story: Mist, then a ridge, then the sun breaking over it, then the descent: one long breath with a single crest at 52 s.

sections.name: open on the valley
sections.action: slow aerial push through moving mist, no editing
sections.music: one held flute note over string harmonics; nothing else enters

sections.name: the ridge appears
sections.action: the ridge resolves out of the mist
sections.music: the flute phrase answers itself a fifth lower; celli enter under it

sections.name: crest
sections.action: the camera clears the ridge; the valley floor opens
sections.music: the low celli move to the tonic; strings widen; the dynamic crest lands at 52 s

sections.name: sun
sections.music: the widest string spread of the cue; the flute holds one long note, then rests

sections.name: descent
sections.action: the camera drops toward the canopy
sections.music: the opening figure inverted, celli only, the mist bed returns

sections.name: final frame
sections.music: solo flute on the tonic, one breath, then the room tail

motifs.name: dawn call
motifs.shape: three rising notes, bare fifth, no vibrato
motifs.returns: answered a fifth lower at 18 s, inverted at 70 s, alone on the tonic at 86 s

hits.why: a movement inside the shot, not an edit: a soft sync, so a few frames either way do not matter

hits.sound: everything sustained stops on the frame; one cello low C enters
hits.why: hard cut to the valley floor; a hard sync point, on the frame. kind cut + sync hard: the sustained voices stop on t with a 15 ms ramp, and the gate skips the level drop within 150 ms of t
the cue's own crest, one beat after the cut so the cut lands first

must_hear: nothing masking 250-3800 Hz while the narration speaks

room_changes.why: the valley floor opens: the room grows and its tail lifts

the room opening as the first light lands
immersive.notes: the sheet records intent; the mix, space and instrument presets execute it. The score's output_targets must name the same deliverables, two-channel first. Presets carry the keyframes, heights and room geometry, never this block.

expression.sonic_picture: Stand in the room: the first ten seconds are a held flute over string harmonics in a wide, damp hall; by the middle a low pulse has entered and never leaves; the last note hangs and is not resolved.
expression.performer: Who plays it and what a human does: the flute breathes in the phrase gaps and swells into the long note; the strings lean on beat one and let the bow ease off before each change.
expression.producer_moves: What a producer does that a score does not say: a slow filter opening over the last sixteen bars, a full stop one beat before the hit, a reverb throw on the last note.
expression.anti_generic: The generic version of this cue is a pad, a four-note arpeggio and a drum loop; what stops it is one pulse that keeps changing and a theme whose leap lands on the weak beat.

theme.contour: arch: a rise of a fifth, a step back, then a fall
theme.interval_character: mostly steps with one leap of a fifth
theme.why_memorable: the leap lands on the weak beat and is never moved
theme.variation_plan: inverted at the return, alone on the tonic at the end

notes: Every field is a target someone can check. feel and avoid_feel are what listen.py tests earshot against; sections is the cue's arc in seconds, and its names are what a trajectory or a room change is anchored to; hits_at is what listen.py looks for in the onset list, and hits is the same moments with a reason and a kind (cut, motion or musical). spatial_staging is the room seen from above: each preset must match its own spot. immersive says whether the field is doing a job, what moves and why, and where the room changes (numbers live in the presets). mix_intent says what must be audible and what must stay free. Write in plain English: earshot reads the words.
